products.note: The strongest common nitrogen bag. Put it on moist soil or work it in so less nitrogen is lost to the air.
The same 46 percent nitrogen as granular urea in smaller beads, used the same way.
Plain granular urea for nitrogen at tillering or early growth, best applied before rain or irrigation rather than on dry hot soil.
Granular urea for fixing pale yellow older leaves caused by low nitrogen.

Ammonium sulfate from the Leyte plant, used for corn, rice and vegetables when both nitrogen and sulfur are short.
Ammonium sulfate for crops that show pale young leaves from low sulfur as well as low nitrogen.
A widely stocked ammonium sulfate brand that supplies nitrogen plus sulfur in one bag.
A cheaper nitrogen source often used on rice and coconut. But avoid it on tobacco and other crops that do not like chloride.

Diammonium phosphate for strong phosphorus at planting on soils that test low.
